purpose: Canonical ordered keyword grammar for the DIO/ODI corpus. It stabilizes lexical identity, preserves conceptual structure, and provides deterministic keyword projections for Zenodo and other metadata surfaces.
principles: Keywords are an ordered metadata grammar, not an unordered bag of tags.
Chunk order is invariant across the corpus and its approved derived artefact profiles.
The identity invariant C0 is always exported in full and always appears first.
C1 is a global candidate vocabulary of reconstruction environments; each object explicitly selects only the environments substantively relevant to that object.
Within master chunks, selected terms retain the same relative order across works.
K6 is exported as a complete ordered block or not exported at all.
Work-specific positioning terms occupy C2 and may vary by work or artefact.
Aliases support recognition but are not exported by default.
Keyword assignment must not retroactively project concepts into an object that the object does not substantively carry.
Exportable metadata surfaces preserve the complete resolved keyword sequence for the relevant object profile whenever the target format supports it; do not create manually curated parallel subsets.

export_policy.flattening_rule: Concatenate active chunks in chunk_order; preserve term order inside each chunk; omit inactive terms; deduplicate case-insensitively without reordering.
export_policy.projection_rule: For a supported metadata surface, resolve and export the complete ordered keyword sequence for the relevant object profile without manual curation. C0 is always complete; C1 is an explicit ordered selection from the global environment candidate pool. Apply a reduced projection only when a verified target-format constraint requires it, and document that deterministic projection separately.
export_policy.c1_selection: Each profile must explicitly list only the C1 reconstruction environments substantively relevant to its object. The literal selector 'all' is not permitted for C1; use an explicit ordered array, including an empty array where none applies.

agentic-er-planner-home.purpose: Product-level semantic profile for the public overview of the design-time Agent Skill.

term_rationales.artificial intelligence: The page describes an AI-agent-proposed identity-changing entity-resolution workflow; it does not describe search-engine, knowledge-graph or human-observer reconstruction.
term_rationales.Agentic Entity Resolution: The product is explicitly designed for agentic entity-resolution workflows.
term_rationales.commit-boundary authorization: The product plans controls around the persistence boundary of proposed identity-changing operations.
term_rationales.identity-changing mutations: Its declared scope includes MERGE, SPLIT, UNMERGE and supported identity-changing OTHER operations.
term_rationales.authorization-eligible evidence: The product distinguishes an agent's proposed match from evidence and conditions eligible to support authorization.
term_rationales.identity-preserving constraints: The planner designs controls intended to prevent unsupported or out-of-scope changes to persistent entity identity.
term_rationales.referential continuity: The investigation includes identity-bearing relationships, affected references and downstream dependencies.
term_rationales.semantic coherence: The planner examines entity context, contradictory claims and whether the proposed identity interpretation is coherent.
term_rationales.entity resolution: Agentic entity resolution is the product's explicit technical domain.
term_rationales.provenance: Evidence origin and provenance are explicit investigation dimensions and planning outputs.

term_rationales.artificial intelligence: The page presents DIO/ODI as a general framework that includes machine-mediated reconstruction by AI systems.
term_rationales.search engines: The page presents the DIO/ODI research foundation, including search-engine reconstruction and AI-mediated search.
term_rationales.knowledge graphs: The page presents the DIO/ODI research foundation across semantic and graph-based identity representations.
term_rationales.human observers: The page presents the DIO/ODI research foundation, which includes human interpretation and reconstruction.
term_rationales.Agentic Entity Resolution: The page explains the research-to-planning application in agentic entity resolution.
term_rationales.commit-boundary authorization: The page explicitly describes the design of the persistent-change boundary and the distinction between recommendation and authorization.
term_rationales.identity-changing mutations: The page names MERGE, SPLIT, UNMERGE and supported identity-changing operations.
term_rationales.authorization-eligible evidence: The workflow explicitly distinguishes provisional evidence from authorization-eligible evidence.
term_rationales.observation domain: The methodology frames entity and domain context as a condition for interpreting the identity proposition.
term_rationales.identity-preserving constraints: The page describes the constraints required before a persistent identity-changing operation can be committed.
term_rationales.referential continuity: The page addresses identity persistence and the relationships involved in identity reconstruction.
term_rationales.semantic coherence: The methodology treats identity, representation, interpretation and reconstruction as connected conditions.
term_rationales.entity resolution: Agentic Entity Resolution is the applied domain to which the page connects the DIO/ODI research.
term_rationales.provenance: The page explicitly treats provenance and source traceability as part of the evidence methodology.

agentic-er-planner-demo.purpose: Semantic profile for the published synthetic CRM MERGE case study and engineering handoff.

term_rationales.artificial intelligence: The page describes an AI-agent-proposed identity-changing entity-resolution workflow; it does not describe search-engine, knowledge-graph or human-observer reconstruction.
term_rationales.Agentic Entity Resolution: The synthetic case starts from an AI agent's proposed CRM account MERGE.
term_rationales.commit-boundary authorization: The plan specifies pre-persistence controls, commit conditions and HOLD requirements.
term_rationales.identity-changing mutations: The example concerns a proposed persistent MERGE of two CRM account identities.
term_rationales.authorization-eligible evidence: The evidence requirements distinguish verified evidence eligible to support authorization from unverified items and agent confidence.
term_rationales.identity-preserving constraints: The parent/holding-company indication must be resolved before a potentially identity-collapsing MERGE can proceed.
term_rationales.referential continuity: The proposed write set includes identity links, related records, history, audit and downstream references.
term_rationales.semantic coherence: The example preserves the distinction between two entities that may be related but not identical.
term_rationales.entity resolution: The synthetic CRM scenario is an entity-resolution case, not a generic CRUD example.
term_rationales.provenance: The planning package records source provenance, evidence provenance and reference provenance.
